items.title: Wake Up at 5
items.notes: Start the day on purpose. If the exact time shifts, the win is waking at the planned time instead of drifting.

items.title: Make My Bed
items.notes: Quick environmental win. Signal that the day has started and the room is not left in chaos.

items.title: Brush My Teeth - Morning
items.notes: Basic hygiene anchor. Keep it boring and automatic.

items.title: Feed Finn & Refill Water
items.notes: Feed Finn and make sure his water is full.

items.title: Take supplements
items.notes: Take prescribed meds and regular supplements consistently.

items.title: Sunlight in the Morning
items.notes: Get outside or near bright natural light early to help energy, mood, and circadian rhythm.

items.title: Outside Before Screens
items.notes: When possible, get outside before recreational screens: sunlight, walk, prayer, yard, or trail. Real world before digital worlds.

items.title: Meditation / Stillness
items.notes: 5-10 minutes of silence, breathing, prayerful stillness, or mindfulness. The goal is calm control, not perfection.

items.title: Read the Bible
items.notes: Read Scripture with attention. Small faithful reading counts more than perfect volume.

items.title: Morning Oath / Pray Alone
items.notes: Pray by yourself honestly. Bring gratitude, stress, repentance, needs, and obedience before God. Speak your values with conviction: husband, father, Christian, leader, disciplined man.

items.title: Help in the Morning
items.notes: Look for one practical way to help the household morning go smoother: girls, dishes, bags, clothes, cleanup, or Megan support.

items.title: Train the Body
items.notes: Lift, walk, cardio, boxing, hike, or another meaningful movement session. On rest days, an intentional walk counts.

items.title: Mobility Workout
items.notes: Mobility routine, stretching, soft tissue, decompression, or recovery work. Keep your body usable, not just strong.

items.title: Daily work review
items.notes: Check team queues, stuck work, volume, and tickets at risk of breaching. Surface what needs action in standup or with the right person.

items.title: Project Work
items.notes: Protected time on high-value work: Knowledge Ecosystem, ServiceNow, KCS, dashboards, process improvement, strategy, or leadership systems.

items.title: Clear Emails
items.notes: Clear or triage work/personal email. Aim for control, not perfection.

items.title: Clear Texts & Messages
items.notes: Clear or triage texts, Teams/Slack, and other important messages that need a response.

items.title: Phone Boundaries Kept
items.notes: Avoid default scrolling, especially during family time, bedtime, and work focus blocks.

items.title: Name It Before I React
items.notes: When triggered, anxious, angry, or impatient, pause and name the emotion: 'I'm feeling ___ because ___.' Then choose the next faithful action.

items.title: Healthy Food Default
items.notes: Prioritize protein, vegetables, reasonable calories, hydration, and mostly healthy foods without letting cravings drive the day. If edibles are used, avoid uncontrolled pantry/freezer spirals and stick to a pre-decided snack or meal.

items.title: Guard the Gate
items.notes: No porn, no edging, no searching, no testing the boundary, and no 'almost porn.' Also avoid upstream triggers like lust-scrolls, thirst traps, and fantasy rabbit holes. If tempted, do one interrupt action: pray, walk, shower, leave the room, message accountability, or go to bed.

items.title: Protein Anchor
items.notes: Hit protein target or include a clear protein source at each main meal. Protein first, cravings second.

items.title: Vegetables With Meals
items.notes: Include vegetables with lunch and dinner, or every main meal when realistic. Greens supplements can support but not replace this habit.

items.title: Walk the Realm
items.notes: Hit step goal or take an intentional walk. On low-energy days, a purposeful walk still counts as movement leadership.

items.title: Boxing / Conditioning Rep
items.notes: Short boxing, bag work, conditioning, intervals, or skill work. Keep it sustainable; it can be a bonus movement rep rather than mandatory hard training.

items.title: Capture Beauty
items.notes: Take one intentional iPhone photo of something meaningful, beautiful, funny, or family-related. Collect moments instead of loot.

items.title: Spend With Wisdom
items.notes: No impulse purchases. Use the 24-hour cart rule for non-urgent items and make spending intentional rather than frictionless.

items.title: End-of-Day Work Shutdown
items.notes: Clear the work to-do list, identify tomorrow's top priorities, close loops, and mentally leave work.

items.title: No Phone Around Girls
items.notes: When you are with Emmy and Liv, be with them. Phone away unless truly needed. This can also count during wider family time when presence matters.

items.title: Ten-Minute Miracle - Emmy
items.notes: At least 10 minutes of focused connection with Emmy. Let her lead when possible. No multitasking.

items.title: Ten-Minute Miracle - Liv
items.notes: At least 10 minutes of focused connection with Liv. Let her lead when possible. No multitasking.

items.title: Emmy Homework / School Growth
items.notes: Homework, reading, school prep, encouragement, or helping Emmy build confidence around school responsibilities.

items.title: Pray Before Dinner
items.notes: Simple family prayer before dinner. Builds household culture, not just personal faith.

items.title: Repair Quickly
items.notes: If you were impatient, distracted, harsh, or disconnected, apologize and reconnect. This is a character habit.

items.title: One Load of Laundry
items.notes: Start, switch, fold, or put away one load. Any meaningful laundry step counts if it moves the household forward.

items.title: Pick Up Dog Poops
items.notes: Keep the yard under control. A daily check counts; pick up when needed. Small unpleasant task that prevents bigger unpleasantness later.

items.title: 10 Minutes Cleaning
items.notes: Clean or reset one area for 10 minutes: kitchen, toys, counters, living room, bedroom, garage, or clutter zone.

items.title: Household Contribution
items.notes: Do one practical home task that actually helps today beyond the automatic basics: dishes, trash, restocking, logistics, cleanup, or support.  Also notice repairs, purchases, scheduling, organizing, and unfinished household loops without waiting to be asked.

items.title: Daily Affection & Pursuit
items.notes: Show Megan warm physical affection and, when appropriate, pursue her playfully or romantically. Keep marriage from becoming only logistics.

items.title: Turn Toward One Bid
items.notes: Notice and respond warmly to at least one connection bid from Megan: comment, question, joke, complaint, touch, request, or invitation.

items.title: Connection Questions
items.notes: Ask Megan something real. Listen without fixing unless she wants solutions. The goal is emotional connection.

items.title: Say Thank You
items.notes: Thank Megan specifically for something she did, carried, handled, or endured. Can also apply to the girls or others when appropriate.

items.title: Serve Megan Unasked
items.notes: Do one thing that lightens her load without needing credit: dishes, girls, cleanup, logistics, bedtime help, or emotional support.

items.title: Read / Learn Something Useful
items.notes: Read, listen, or learn for 20 minutes. The win is not just consuming content but taking away one useful insight for faith, marriage, parenting, fitness, work, or life.

items.title: Stop When Bored
items.notes: If gaming becomes boredom, obligation, checklist clearing, or 'one more thing,' stop. Boredom is the cue to exit, not grind harder.

items.title: Evening Shutdown / Tomorrow Prep
items.notes: Close loops, prep for tomorrow, reduce phone stimulation, check calendar, and make the next morning easier.

items.title: Daily Values Review
items.notes: Ask: Did I live like the man I say I want to be? Note one win and one adjustment. Best done later in the day if morning feels too early.

items.title: Lights-Out Consistency
items.notes: Get in bed on time and protect the sleep window. This is tracked separately because sleep is foundational.

items.title: Clear Physical Mail & Paper Clutter
items.notes: Open, toss, file, or act on physical mail and small paper clutter so it does not become background stress.

items.title: Note for Megan
items.notes: Write her a note, text, card, or voice memo that encourages her specifically.

items.title: Practice Photography / iPhone Mastery
items.notes: Take, edit, organize, or intentionally practice photography. Prioritize low-friction iPhone mastery unless you intentionally choose to practice with the camera.

items.title: Family Adventure / Intentional Outing
items.notes: Do something intentional with the family: park, walk, hike, library, breakfast, church event, movie night, backyard game, board/card game, or outdoor outing.

items.title: Game-Free / Sabbath Rhythm
items.notes: One intentional block or day where gaming does not lead. Prioritize worship, family, rest, reading, outside time, recovery, or Oathforge execution over app/game refinement.

items.title: Weekly Life Review
items.notes: Review habits, habit cards/tasks, calendar, misses, wins, family needs, work priorities, and what needs to change next week. Look for friction, not just failure.

items.title: Marriage Date / Connection Block
items.notes: Plan intentional time with Megan: date night, at-home date, walk, coffee, shared activity, or deeper conversation.

items.title: Fair Play / Household Ownership Check
items.notes: Ask: What am I fully owning from conception to planning to execution, not just helping with?

items.title: Family Memory Capture
items.notes: Save photos, print pictures, write down funny kid moments, update an album, preserve family memories, or use iPhone photography to capture real life with the girls.  Also save funny quotes, milestone videos, school art, traditions, and print or organize favorite memories.

items.title: Friendship / Hospitality Touchpoint
items.notes: Invite someone over, plan a hangout, schedule a call, or invest in another couple/family/friendship.

items.title: Home Declutter Zone
items.notes: Pick one zone: drawer, closet, toys, garage shelf, office, clothes, pantry, bathroom, etc. Finish one contained area.

items.title: Family Protection Review
items.notes: Review insurance coverage, beneficiaries, emergency information, estate documents, important account access, and unresolved family administrative needs. Turn any gaps into concrete next actions.  Also review passwords, shared documents, utilities, taxes, registrations, renewals, beneficiaries, and emergency information.

items.title: Reset Ritual
items.notes: The bridge out of the window: stand up, water, two-minute walk, review the next task. This transition prevents the second session better than any rule.

items.title: Monthly Review
items.notes: One sit-down, three lenses: (1) Identity - who am I becoming, are the four roles being lived? (2) Oathforge Audit - is the app serving the habits or replacing them? (3) 30-Day Household Reset - what needs a reset next month?

items.title: Log Meals & Weigh In
items.notes: Built With Science ritual: morning weigh-in + log every meal. You did this religiously once - the data kept you honest. Weigh first thing; log as you eat, not from memory at night.

items.title: Steward’s Weekly Review
items.notes: Walk the 25 areas at the week’s start — Notice · Plan · Execute · Close the Loop. Plans forge quests automatically.

items.title: One Intentional Touchpoint
items.notes: Ping one direct report about THEIR thing - not a status ask, just presence. Rotate through the team so Friday's gut check is already answered.

items.title: Recognize One Person (Specific Praise)
items.notes: One specific, named praise - Slack counts. Name the exact action and its impact. Specific beats grand.

items.title: Clear One Blocker
items.notes: Remove one obstacle for someone on the team today - an approval, an escalation, a decision they're waiting on.

items.title: Ask Before Answering
items.notes: Ask one good question before giving one answer. Coach the thinking, don't just dispense the fix.
